original_abstract.text: Training-free expert pruning makes two decisions: which experts to remove, and what the layer computes when its router still selects a removed expert. Published methods change both at once. Holding the mask fixed, we compare replacement operators from three families on OLMoE, DeepSeek-V2-Lite and Moonlight, with Granite as a fourth router, using paired, multiplicity-corrected tests. The largest effect is a choice usually left implicit: the survivors' gate scale. On routers trained without top-k renormalization, renormalizing the survivors' gates, a common implementation choice, costs 0.8-8.5 points and reverses whether rerouting beats MoNE's mean-output replacement; on two routers trained with renormalization, the trained scale wins at 50% pruning. We introduce the tilted novice, a closed-form low-rank map of the pruned expert's input whose rank-0 case is MoNE's constant. At 50% pruning it adds 1.2-1.8% parameters and gains 3.45 and 1.37 points over the constant on OLMoE and Moonlight, stable across calibration draws and largely unchanged by 4- and 3-bit quantization. No operator dominates: trained-scale rerouting is best on DeepSeek-V2-Lite, and a partial copy of each pruned expert is statistically indistinguishable from the tilted novice on two models. Evaluation can change conclusions: at 25% pruning MoNE's constant keeps 92-97% of dense multiple-choice accuracy but only 5-65% of GSM8K and 0-17% of code scores, and the calibration domain moves the mask 4-9 times more than resampling. We propose a five-item reporting checklist.
original_abstract.source_title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning

zh.text: 固定专家裁剪集合，单独比较被裁专家的替代计算与剩余专家的门控缩放，揭示路由实现对裁剪收益的影响。提出低秩输入映射tilted novice，在OLMoE和Moonlight上优于常量替代，为稀疏模型压缩时保留路由语义和选择校准方案提供依据。

en.text: Holds pruning masks fixed to isolate replacement operators and surviving-expert gate scales. Introduces the tilted novice, a closed-form low-rank input map that improves over constant replacement on OLMoE and Moonlight. Experiments show that preserving trained routing scale and choosing calibration data materially affect pruning results, informing practical sparse-model compression.

original_abstract.text: Gated Delta Networks (GDNs) offer linear-time sequence modeling, yet long-context prefill remains costly due to dense intra-chunk computation, recurrent-state updates, and intermediate state storage. We introduce SparseGDN, a hardware-aware framework that combines structured intra-chunk approximation with input-dependent recurrent-event selection while producing outputs for every token. A block-adjacent solver reduces local Delta-solve computation, while a dynamic selector allocates recurrent-update budgets across head pairs. The GPU implementation materializes updates only for selected events and reconstructs token outputs using compact state snapshots and group-local interactions, reducing computation and memory traffic. We evaluate SparseGDN on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B across RULER tasks and context lengths from 4K to 128K. Retaining approximately 29% of recurrent events on average, SparseGDN achieves 1.50-1.94x GDN-core prefill speedups over native FLA kernels, including online selection overhead.
original_abstract.source_title: SparseGDN: Chunk Sparse in Linear Attention

zh.text: 用块邻接近似减少局部Delta求解，再按输入动态选择递归更新事件，并通过紧凑状态快照重建全部token输出。Qwen3.5的4B和9B实验平均保留约29%的递归事件，在4K至128K上下文获得1.50至1.94倍GDN核心预填充加速，包含在线选择开销。

en.text: Combines a block-adjacent Delta solver with input-dependent recurrent-event selection, reconstructing every token output from compact state snapshots. On Qwen3.5-4B and 9B, retaining about 29% of recurrent events yields 1.50–1.94x GDN-core prefill speedups over native FLA kernels across 4K–128K contexts, including online selection overhead.

original_abstract.text:
Modern recommender models scale sparse representations and dense computation together. They process thousands of heterogeneous feature fields, long user-behavior sequences, and trillion-scale Embedding parameters, while their dense networks increasingly use large Transformer architectures. The resulting execution mismatch creates fine-grained operations within stages, load imbalance and synchronization delays across devices, and GPU resource bubbles between stages. As models grow, these costs become a primary limit to scalable recommender training. Although existing systems improve Embedding caching and data prefetching, these inefficiencies still coexist in the GPU-centric workloads we study and jointly limit end-to-end throughput.
  We present RecIS, a unified framework for GPU-centric recommender training. RecIS treats the complete path from input features to dense computation as one optimization target and coordinates three complementary mechanisms. First, adaptive fusion combines fragmented feature transformations with vectorized memory access. Second, a GPU Embedding engine uses hash-based sharding and hierarchical communication to balance request placement and eliminate redundant transfers; it also specializes aggregation for forward and backward index structures. Third, a multistage pipeline overlaps input preparation for future iterations with dense computation in the current iteration. Together, these mechanisms reorganize a fragmented sparse front end into a dataflow that continuously feeds dense computation.
  We evaluate RecIS on representative industrial recommender models across distributed training platforms. Compared with PICASSO and TorchRec, RecIS reaches up to $2.62\times$ and $1.15\times$ their throughput, respectively, while reducing step latency by up to 61.5\% and 12.9\%. RecIS provides an efficient and scalable training system for large recommender models.
original_abstract.source_title: RecIS: Unifying Sparse and Dense Computation for Efficient Recommendation Training

zh.text: 面向大规模推荐训练，统一优化特征处理、稀疏嵌入与稠密网络之间的执行开销。通过自适应算子融合、GPU嵌入分片与分层通信，以及多阶段流水线减少同步和资源空闲；实验吞吐最高达到PICASSO的2.62倍、TorchRec的1.15倍，为稀疏与稠密模型共同扩展提供系统支持。

en.text: Coordinates feature processing, sparse embeddings and dense networks for scalable recommendation training. Adaptive feature-operation fusion, GPU embedding sharding with hierarchical communication, and multistage pipelining reduce synchronization and idle resources. Reported throughput reaches up to 2.62x PICASSO and 1.15x TorchRec, supporting joint sparse-and-dense model scaling.

original_abstract.text: Residual connections underpin Transformers, but they implicitly tie the residual width carried through depth to the compute width used inside each layer. We introduce Hierarchical Residuals (HiRes), a minimalist architectural change that decouples these dimensions, widening the residual state while keeping per-layer compute width fixed. HiRes groups layers into blocks: standard d-dimensional PreNorm layers operate inside each block, while a wider D-dimensional PostNorm outer residual connects blocks. Learned read/write projections bridge the two spaces at block boundaries, leaving individual Transformer layers unchanged. Across different model sizes and depths, HiRes consistently outperforms vanilla residual addition, with fitted scaling laws indicating a 1.30-fold improvement in FLOPs efficiency. On OLMoE-1B-7B pretraining for 500B tokens, HiRes achieves 0.0208 lower training loss and 1.14-point higher downstream accuracy. HiRes is also competitive with other residual expansion methods such as VWN, mHC and AttnRes with less activation memory and I/O costs. Built from only dense projections and normalizations, it requires neither specialized kernels nor infrastructure-level optimizations. HiRes thus exposes residual width as a practical scaling variable using only standard operators.
original_abstract.source_title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width

en.text: HiRes separates residual-state width from per-layer compute width: narrow Transformer layers operate inside blocks, while learned read/write projections connect a wider outer residual stream. Experiments report 1.30× FLOPs efficiency from fitted scaling laws and a 1.14-point downstream gain for OLMoE-1B-7B after 500B training tokens. This provides a practical capacity-scaling direction for Transformer rankers without widening every layer; CTR gains remain untested.

zh.text: HiRes 将残差状态宽度与单层计算宽度解耦：块内使用较窄的 Transformer 层，通过可学习的读写投影连接更宽的外层残差流。实验拟合的缩放规律显示 FLOPs 效率提升至 1.30 倍，OLMoE-1B-7B 在训练 500B token 后的下游准确率提升 1.14 个百分点。该方法为 Transformer 排序模型提供了无需加宽每层的容量扩展方向，但尚未验证 CTR 收益。

original_abstract.text: Looped language models can strengthen reasoning through repeated computation with shared weights, increasing execution depth without adding independent parameters. However, each additional pass increases training floating-point operations (FLOPs), making these gains more expensive to obtain. To address this cost, we propose UpLoop, a pretraining schedule that uses upcycling to train looped Transformers while exactly matching a standard dense baseline in final parameter count, total training tokens, and training FLOPs. Specifically, UpLoop begins with a shallow Transformer, progressively grows its depth by copying learned layers, and uses the computation saved early to support repeated execution of a shared middle block later in training. Experiments across model scales show improvements in language modeling and downstream performance, with the average score across 22 downstream tasks increasing from 22.99 to 27.52 at 1.3B parameters. These gains also extend to mathematical reasoning after supervised fine-tuning.
original_abstract.source_title: UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute

zh.text: 先训练较浅网络，再复制已学习层逐步增加深度，将前期节省的计算用于后期共享中间层的循环执行。与普通Transformer匹配最终参数量、训练token和训练FLOPs后，1.3B模型在22项任务上的均分从22.99提升到27.52，为固定预算下的深度扩展提供训练方案。

en.text: Starts with a shallow Transformer, grows it by copying learned layers, and spends the saved early compute on repeated execution of a shared middle block. With final parameters, training tokens and FLOPs matched to a dense baseline, the 1.3B model improves its mean score over 22 tasks from 22.99 to 27.52, providing a compute-budgeted depth-scaling schedule.

original_abstract.text: Tabular transformer models such as TabPFN achieve strong predictive performance but incur substantial inference costs, making them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained settings. While looped transformers reduce parameter count through weight sharing, they can lose significant predictive power when stopped early. To address this challenge, we introduce the Elastically Looped Tabular Transformer (ElTab), a single model trained to operate across different computational budgets through supervision at randomly sampled early exits. Across 30 OpenML classification datasets, a single ElTab model matches six depth-specific looped models while cutting training cost by more than half, and matches a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. These results show that elastic-depth training yields a single model that adapts to the deployment budget at hand, offering a favorable trade-off among predictive performance, storage, and computational cost.

en.text: ElTab trains one looped tabular Transformer with randomly sampled early exits to serve multiple compute budgets. Across 30 OpenML classification datasets it matches six depth-specific looped models with less than half their training cost and matches a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline using 25% fewer inference FLOPs.

zh.text: ElTab通过随机采样提前退出位置训练一个循环表格Transformer，使同一模型适配多种计算预算。在30个OpenML分类数据集上，以不足一半训练成本匹配六个独立深度模型，并以少25%的推理FLOPs匹配12层TabPFN式基线。

original_abstract.text: Transformers retain an explicit history of the sequence, allowing attention to directly retrieve past representations. However, the size of the KV-Cache and the cost of a new token increase with the context length. State Space Models compress the past into a fixed-size recurrent state, at the cost of reduced addressability. We present the Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT), a hybrid architecture that separates sequence encoding from information reading. The encoder uses several memory units, each implemented by a dynamical system with a complex diagonal recurrent matrix. An input-dependent leak rate controls their updates. The decoder then uses attention to read and combine their outputs, without going through the token history. The formulation of the recurrence allows an associative scan with O(T ) total work and O(log T ) parallel depth, with fixed dimensions. During autoregressive inference, the recurrent states and the convolution cache remain fixed in size. We compare DMT with Mamba and Transformer on cognitive and language modeling tasks, and show its strengths and limitations: DMT achieves the best results on several cognitive tasks and language modeling performance close to that of Transformer, but remains behind Mamba in language modeling. On selective copy, DMT also shows stronger length extrapolation than Mamba and Transformer. These results demonstrate that parallel dynamical memory units are a promising mechanism for retaining and using information over sequences.
original_abstract.source_title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention

zh.text: 将序列编码与信息读取分离：多个带输入相关更新率的递归记忆单元压缩历史，再由注意力读取这些单元的当前输出。固定维度下采用线性总工作量的并行扫描，推理状态大小保持固定；认知任务与选择性复制显示优势，语言建模接近Transformer而落后于Mamba，为长序列记忆设计提供参考。

en.text: Separates recurrent sequence encoding from attention-based reading of memory-unit outputs. Input-dependent updates and diagonal complex recurrence permit linear-work associative scans with fixed-size inference state. Cognitive tasks and selective-copy extrapolation show benefits; language modeling is close to the evaluated Transformer but trails Mamba, offering an alternative long-sequence memory design.

original_abstract.text: Linear attention scales linearly with sequence length, but its finite-state memory can limit long-context retrieval. In gated linear recurrences, memory retention depends on state decay, which is shaped jointly by gate parameters A_log and dt_bias and by input activations. In controlled Gated DeltaNet (GDN) experiments, both parameters remain highly correlated with their initial values after training, highlighting the importance of initialization. Therefore, we introduce Dual-Axis Memory Initialization (DAMI), which jointly configures these parameters before training. DAMI assigns geometric timescales across heads for varied retrieval distances and a low-high-low input-sensitivity profile across layers. A small activation sample calibrates the GDN-family implementation to match both behavioral targets without adding trainable parameters. Across GDN, KDA, GDN2, Mamba-2, and RWKV-7, DAMI improves average RULER-style retrieval accuracy by 5.29 to 16.71 percentage points over the corresponding random-initialization baselines. Performance on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and 2K real-world retrieval remains broadly comparable to those baselines. Our code is available at https://speedai.com/research/dami.
original_abstract.source_title: DAMI: Dual-Axis Memory Initialization for Enhanced Long-Context Retrieval in Gated Linear Attention

zh.text: 在训练前联合设置门控线性注意力的衰减参数，使不同头覆盖不同记忆时间尺度，并沿深度配置输入敏感度。小规模激活校准无需新增可训练参数，在GDN、KDA、Mamba-2等架构上提升长距离检索准确率5.29至16.71个百分点，可参考用于长行为序列记忆初始化。

en.text: Jointly initializes decay parameters to distribute memory timescales across heads and input sensitivity across depth. Small activation samples calibrate the initialization without adding trainable parameters. Reported RULER-style retrieval gains span 5.29–16.71 percentage points across gated recurrent architectures, suggesting an initialization strategy for long-history memory.

original_abstract.text: Looping re-applies a block of layers so that each token passes through the block more than once. Adding a loop to a trained model is attractive because it leaves the parameter count, and hence the disk size, the memory footprint and the training cost unchanged. Unfortunately, every generated token pays for the loop. Re-applying m of N layers makes each token about (N+m)/N times as expensive. Loops that a model learns during large-scale pretraining justify this price, but whether loops added after pretraining justify this cost remains unclear. We compare a looped model with two simple baselines. We first compare it with the same model trained identically without the loop (equal parameters). Secondly, we compare it with the best unlooped use of the same inference floating-point operations (equal FLOPs). Across Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B parameters, only the looped 0.8B model beats both baselines. At 4B and 9B, the looped model does not beat the first baseline, i.e. the same model trained without the loop. This is not because the benchmarks are too easy, since on the same benchmarks the unlooped 9B model still scores up to 13 points higher than the 4B model, showing that there is ample room for improvement. Introducing loops in an already pretrained model therefore only pays for small models with a fixed parameter budget.
original_abstract.source_title: There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?

zh.text: 研究给已训练模型添加共享层循环是否值得额外推理计算，同时设置等参数与等推理FLOPs基线。在Qwen3和Qwen3.5的0.8B至9B实验中，仅0.8B循环模型同时超过两类基线，为循环深度扩展的成本评估提供直接对照方法。

en.text: Evaluates post-hoc layer looping against both equal-parameter and equal-inference-FLOP baselines. Across tested Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models from 0.8B to 9B, only the 0.8B looped model beats both baselines. The controlled comparisons provide a practical methodology for assessing the compute return of shared-depth scaling.

original_abstract.text: The quadratic scaling of attention is a fundamental bottleneck limiting the long-context capabilities of large language models (LLMs). A variety of approaches have attempted to circumvent this, but they either fail to match attention's expressiveness (e.g., sliding-window or linear attention variants with fixed-size state) or only achieve constant-factor speedups (e.g., sparse attention methods whose indexers themselves scale quadratically). In this paper, we derive an asymptotically subquadratic sparse attention method based on a hierarchical, tree-structured indexer, which we call Zyphra Hierarchical Attention (ZHA). ZHA constructs a tree of recursively compressed key summaries over the KV cache, which future queries traverse from the top down to retrieve a sparse subset of keys. Crucially, by iteratively growing the tree's depth, the total cost including routing and final attention grows sublinearly in sequence length, resulting in overall subquadratic (but superlinear) scaling for attention. We demonstrate that ZHA can be cheaply applied to existing pretrained models with only a short KL distillation training stage of a billion tokens, and maintains performance on long-context retrieval and challenging reasoning, mathematical, and agentic coding evaluation tasks. Moreover, we show that our method is highly robust to tree geometry including very deep trees of up to 6 levels. Finally, we develop a detailed performance model and show that our approach scales subquadratically, dramatically outperforms competing methods beyond 1 million tokens of context, and ultimately has the potential to extend effective context windows to the hundreds of millions or billions of tokens.
original_abstract.source_title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer

zh.text: ZHA将KV摘要组织为树，自顶向下检索键，使索引与注意力整体呈次二次计算增长。修订版将适配已有模型的KL蒸馏规模明确为10亿token，并报告保留所测检索与推理能力；百万token以上的速度优势来自性能模型推算。

en.text: ZHA builds a tree of compressed KV summaries and retrieves keys top-down, giving subquadratic indexing and attention cost. The revision specifies a one-billion-token KL-distillation stage to adapt pretrained models while retaining evaluated retrieval and reasoning capabilities. Advantages beyond one million context tokens are projections from a performance model.

original_abstract.text: Decision models target structured tasks by directly predicting choices or scores, avoiding autoregressive decoding latency. However, transferring a generative LLM's ranking knowledge to a decision model remains challenging: the teacher expresses preferences through a ranked list of document ID sequences, while the student determines the ranking using scores from the first-token position. To bridge this gap, we introduce DecisionRank, a decision model trained through item-space on-policy distillation (OPD). Item-space OPD constructs the student's rollout by sorting its document scores into a ranked sequence. A generative teacher takes the resulting ranking list as inputs and provides conditional feedback to directly supervise those scores. Combined with offline ranking supervision, DecisionRank achieves state-of-the-art performance on both general and reasoning-intensive retrieval benchmarks such as TREC DL, BEIR, and BRIGHT. Across four benchmarks, item-space OPD consistently outperforms alternative training objectives. Even at 1.7B parameters, DecisionRank surpasses its 27B generative teacher on TREC DL19--23. At 8B, it outperforms its generative listwise counterpart while running $24.5\times$ faster on TREC DL and $16.7\times$ faster on BRIGHT.
original_abstract.source_title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers

zh.text: 将学生对文档的首token打分排序为列表，再由生成式教师沿该排序给出条件反馈，实现物品空间的在策略蒸馏。1.7B模型在TREC DL19–23超过27B教师；8B模型相对生成式列表重排在TREC DL和BRIGHT分别加速24.5倍和16.7倍，为低延迟重排提供训练路径。

en.text: Sorts student first-token document scores into a ranking and obtains conditional feedback from a generative teacher for item-space on-policy distillation. A 1.7B student surpasses its 27B teacher on TREC DL19–23; the 8B model runs 24.5x faster on TREC DL and 16.7x faster on BRIGHT than its generative listwise counterpart, supporting efficient reranking.

original_abstract.text: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. N-LSA matches the accuracy of full attention with a training speedup of 1.6x per layer at 128k tokens. LSA offers practical and efficient attention for models to benefit from ultra-long context.
original_abstract.source_title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention

zh.text: 将键向量在学习得到的潜在空间中分层聚类，查询沿簇层级选择候选，减少超长上下文的索引成本。提供蒸馏和原生训练两种方案；1000万token实验报告单层注意力加速，原生方案在128K长度下实现单层训练1.6倍加速，可借鉴于超长行为序列的稀疏检索。

en.text: Clusters keys hierarchically in a learned latent space so queries select clusters rather than score every key. Distilled and natively trained variants improve ultra-long-context attention; reported 10M-token speedups concern individual attention layers, while native training achieves a 1.6x per-layer speedup at 128K. The indexer offers a design reference for long-history retrieval.
